clue.text: Expert's statement of the obvious, temperature-wise

definitions.meaning: an expert is an ace, a star performer; the 's reads as 'is', joining the two halves
split as ..., a truism about heat: something warm is warm

explanation.surface: A specialist pronounces, with great authority, that the weather is hot.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotshot is a slang term for a highly skilled, successful person, an ace.

clue.text: Salutation to man making hostile takeover

parts.note: hi is a greeting
Jack is a man's name, and jack a generic word for a man

explanation.surface: Greeting a man who is mounting a hostile corporate bid.
explanation.definitionFit: A hijack is the forcible seizure of a vehicle or, figuratively, a takeover against the owners' will.

clue.text: Blowing part of our capital

definitions.meaning: sounding a horn or whistle
A district of south London, the setter's capital

explanation.surface: A gale blowing through part of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'our capital' is London, as The Times is a London paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Tooting is sounding a horn, and also the name of a London district.

clue.text: Something worn on top in temple, say

definitions.meaning: a helmet or hat covering the head
the temple is a part, or piece, of the head

explanation.surface: Someone wears a ceremonial headdress in a place of worship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'temple' suggests a place of worship; it is the side of the skull.
explanation.definitionFit: A headpiece is a hat or helmet, and read literally a piece of the head such as the temple.

clue.text: The kind of list that's a bother

definitions.meaning: a ... list of tasks still to be done
a fuss or commotion

explanation.surface: A remark that keeping a list of chores is a nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: A to-do list records pending tasks, and a to-do is also a fuss or commotion.

clue.text: With a cry, I'll somehow become expressive of emotion

indicators.note: somehow says the letters of the words a cry and I'll come together in some new order

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored, giving the three letters I, L, L

explanation.surface: Someone who cries out finds themselves becoming emotional.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyrical writing or speech pours out feeling, as a song lyric does.

clue.text: Survive with very little, just in time

parts.note: to last is to endure, keep going
minute means tiny

explanation.surface: Getting by on almost nothing until the deadline.
explanation.definitionFit: Something last-minute happens at the latest possible moment, only just in time.

clue.text: Receiver's run not quite so long

definitions.note: the 's reads as 'is', so the definition is just a receiver, a set picking up broadcasts

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: not quite means one letter short of the whole, so the last letter goes

parts.note: adios is Spanish for goodbye, so long

explanation.surface: A football receiver's run wasn't quite as long as hoped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' trims the last S from ADIOS.
explanation.definitionFit: A radio is an apparatus that receives broadcast signals.

clue.text: Firm's car is damaged in mountainous island

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: damaged signals the letters of car is are knocked out of their order

explanation.surface: A company car is wrecked on a mountain road.
explanation.definitionFit: Corsica is a rugged, mountainous French island in the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Sees what someone is saying

parts.note: 'see what you mean' usually means understand; here it is literal, reading speech from mouth movements

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who lip-reads understands speech by watching the speaker's mouth rather than hearing it.

clue.text: Threatened one in awfully jaded prose

indicators.note: in places the numeral piece within the rearranged letters of the prose words
awfully says the letters of jaded prose are badly arranged and must be reworked

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Someone felt menaced by a piece of tired, clichéd writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' rearranges JADED PROSE into JEOPARDSED, and 'in' puts I (one) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To jeopardise something is to put it at risk, so jeopardised means threatened or endangered.

clue.text: Material for curtains in theatre

definitions.meaning: ... (or repp) is a ribbed fabric used for upholstery and drapes
short for repertory, a theatre company performing a rotating set of plays

explanation.surface: The fabric for the stage curtains in a playhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Rep is a ribbed furnishing fabric, and also short for repertory theatre.

clue.text: Chap working on deal, perhaps, is irritable

definitions.meaning: deal is pine or fir timber, so the man working it is a carpenter
touchy, quick to take offence

explanation.surface: A man busy at a business deal turns out to be bad-tempered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deal' looks like a business transaction; here it is softwood timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Chippy is British slang for a carpenter, and also means touchy or prickly, quick to bristle.

clue.text: I am West of city in Alabama, still

indicators.note: in an across answer, west means to the left, so this piece comes first

parts.note: I am contracts to I'M
Mobile is a port city in Alabama

explanation.surface: Someone announces they live just west of a city in Alabama, still.
explanation.definitionFit: Something immobile cannot move, so it stays still and motionless.

clue.text: Game in which the loser can barely finish

definitions.text: Game in which the loser can barely finish

parts.words: Game in which the loser can barely finish
parts.note: barely means scarcely, but literally naked: the loser here sheds clothing until bare

explanation.definitionFit: In this card game players who lose hands remove garments, so the loser ends up naked.

clue.text: His heart, possibly, is in message of good wishes

parts.note: read as Hi's, the plural of hi: several hellos, i.e. greetings
a heart is one example of a playing card

explanation.surface: A man's heart may be expressed in a card sending love and good wishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'His' is not a pronoun but HI'S, plural hellos.
explanation.definitionFit: A greetings card is the folded card one sends to convey good wishes on a birthday or holiday.

clue.text: Information in spread for use of weapons

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the word for spread

parts.note: to splay is to spread out
word means news, information

explanation.surface: News within a report on the fencing contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Swordplay is the skilled use of swords, fencing.

clue.text: Lift a short distance

definitions.meaning: steal; Cockney rhyming slang for pinch, to steal
half of an inch is a tiny length

explanation.surface: Raise something only slightly.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang replaces a word with a rhyming phrase: half-inch rhymes with pinch, meaning steal.
explanation.definitionFit: Half-inch is rhyming slang meaning to steal, and literally a tiny measurement.

clue.text: Cav and Pag, for example, in forms requiring fewer characters

definitions.meaning: the operas Cavalleria Rusticana and Pagliacci are nicknamed Cav and Pag, shortened titles
shortened written forms use fewer letters

explanation.surface: Opera fans' nicknames for two short operas in a double bill, shorter to write.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' suggests roles in the operas, but means letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Shortened versions of words or titles are contractions, written with fewer letters than the full form.

clue.text: Unfinished two-master turning up a great deal in port

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter is lopped off

parts.note: a brig is a two-masted sailing ship

indicators.note: in a down answer, turning up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: lots means a great deal

explanation.surface: An incomplete sailing ship turns up a big cargo at harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfinished' cuts BRIG to BRI, and 'turning up' turns LOTS into STOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Bristol is a historic port city in south-west England.

clue.text: Slim son, one making advances

parts.note: a lender advances money

explanation.surface: A thin son pesters people with romantic advances.
explanation.definitionFit: Slender means slim, thin.

clue.text: Minister to put in an appearance

definitions.meaning: care for, look after
be present at

explanation.surface: A clergyman going to show up somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minister' looks like a noun, a cleric; it is a verb, to tend.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend means both to care for someone and to be present at an event.

clue.text: Cleaned-up document showing jury's conclusion on reasonable arrest

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece written on another follows it, so this tail comes after

parts.note: fair means reasonable, just
cop as a noun means an arrest, as in 'it's a fair cop'

indicators.note: conclusion points to the final letter of the word jury's

explanation.surface: A tidied record of a trial shows the jury's verdict on a justified arrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's a fair cop' is British slang said by a criminal admitting a justified arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: A fair copy is a neat final version of a document with corrections made.

clue.text: Effortlessly move players around Oval

indicators.note: around says the cast surround the next piece

parts.note: the cast are the actors
O is oval in shape

explanation.surface: Players move easily around the Oval cricket ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oval is a London cricket ground; here it is just the shape of the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: To coast is to move along without effort, like a freewheeling bicycle.

clue.text: Least hard-working learner that is put outside

indicators.note: the phrase for that is is placed around the learner letter

parts.note: id est, Latin for 'that is', abbreviated i.e.
L, the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: The laziest pupil gets sent out of the classroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Idlest is the superlative of idle, meaning most lazy, doing the least work.

clue.text: Prison caused change of heart — that's the aim

indicators.note: the heart of a four-letter word is its middle two letters, which are swapped

parts.note: gaol is the British spelling of jail

explanation.surface: Prison made someone change their mind, and that was the point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change of heart' swaps the middle letters AO of GAOL to OA.
explanation.definitionFit: A goal is an aim or objective.

clue.text: Head organized teachers

definitions.meaning: slang for the head
the National Union of Teachers, a British trade union

explanation.surface: A head teacher runs a staff of well-organised teachers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' suggests a headteacher; it is slang for the cranium. The NUT was Britain's main teachers' union.
explanation.definitionFit: Nut is informal for the head, and the initials of the former National Union of Teachers.

clue.text: Admit strange lack restricting fashionable side

indicators.note: restricting means holding in, so the rearranged letters enclose the next piece
strange says the letters of lack are rearranged

parts.note: now means trendy, in fashion
an edge is a side or border

explanation.surface: To confess a peculiar shortage of trendy attitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' gives ACKL, which then holds the word for fashionable before the side is added.
explanation.definitionFit: To acknowledge something is to admit or recognise it as true.

clue.text: Composer, with hesitation, put gun away

parts.note: Gustav Holst, English composer of The Planets
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A composer hesitates before laying his gun aside.
explanation.definitionFit: To holster a pistol is to put it into its leather case, its belt sheath.

clue.text: Unusual early edition with multilevel style

indicators.note: unusual signals the letters of early are put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A rare first printing with a tiered design.
explanation.definitionFit: A layered style, as in a haircut, is cut at different lengths in several tiers.
